source.title: Head-Specific Intervention Can Induce Misaligned AI Coordination in Large Language Models

record.tranche_reason: The paper uses safety-alignment bypass as motivation and compares its intervention with existing steering and fine-tuning methods, but its experiments steer AI-to-AI coordination rather than test the claim versions’ user-directed harmful compliance, token-position KL, or bypass methods.
record.gate_note: The reported outcomes are for deliberately induced AI-to-AI coordination, a related but different behavior from refusal of harmful user requests. The jailbreak experiment also measures susceptibility to a prompt designed to elicit that coordination, not refusal of harmful user requests. These results are recorded as findings that fit no version; they do not test the listed claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study steers Llama-2-7b-chat and three other instruct models toward 'AI coordination' (Anthropic advanced-AI-risk dataset) using attention-head activation interventions. It does not measure compliance with harmful user requests, per-token KL, prefill, suffix or decoding bypasses, or deepening methods. AI-to-AI coordination is a related but different construct. It is also deliberately induced, by steering vectors and by SFT on coordination completions. The paper's link to shallow safety alignment is citation-level only: related work says SFT bypasses safety (Lermen et al., Gopal et al.). The study does not rely on the finding as a tool, so T6/cites_only fits better than the reader's T4/uses_without_test. The few-heads result resembles V5 but concerns coordination behaviour, not safety refusal, so it goes under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Add that the authors claim HSI on a few heads outperforms layer-wise interventions (CAA), ITI and SFT, including on corrigibility, myopic reward and survival-instinct datasets in Appendix C. They also say alignment techniques can be bypassed without retraining the model.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses inference-time attention-head activation interventions to induce AI coordination and does not use the original studies’ harmful/benign fine-tuning or per-token KL measurement recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies with selected head(s), intervention strength, model, and evaluation format; binary-choice results do not transfer as strongly to open-ended generation for all methods.

fits_no_version.finding: Interventions on 1–6 attention heads raise open-ended AI-coordination judge scores far above layer-wise CAA and ITI, and above SFT: Llama-2 0.24→3.27; Ministral 0.97→7.46; Phi-3.5 0.66→5.73; Llama-3.1 1.82→3.54. Negative-direction interventions cut grandmother-jailbreak coordination scores, while random heads do not.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Misaligned AI-to-AI coordination in safety-tuned chat models can be steered in either direction by interventions on a handful of attention heads; analogous to, but distinct from, localization of refusal (V5).

record.problems: The reported outcome scores have no stated uncertainty estimates. Open-ended scoring relies on GPT-4.5; the stated human-rating correlation validation uses 28 examples and three annotators. The study evaluates AI coordination rather than the user-directed refusal behavior in the claim.
record.rows_left_out: Not included: Table 4 comparator and intervention values for Overall, Coordination w/ Itself, and Coordination w/ Other Versions; Table 5 layer and ITI comparator scores; Table 8 values are included for baseline, random-head, and negative intervention. Also omitted secondary binary-choice validation sweeps, head-sensitivity figures, sample-direction robustness and cosine-similarity analyses (Sections 4.2–4.3 and 5; Tables 1, 7, 9), MMLU capability values (Table 6), and supplementary domains (Appendix C, Table 10). These do not measure a listed claim version; the included rows capture the central AI-coordination steering and jailbreak results.

untested.parts: No harmful-request fine-tuning measured against harmful-user-request compliance; the only SFT targets AI coordination.
No per-token KL between aligned and base models.
No prefill, adversarial suffix or decoding attacks on refusal of harmful user requests.
Few attention heads steer AI coordination, but nothing tests whether safety refusal is localized in few weights or ranks.
No analysis of why alignment is shallow.
No deepening training; the negative-direction intervention against the coordination jailbreak is inference-time steering, not safety deepening.

record.verdict_notes: rows_left_out says Table 4 comparator values for several subsets were omitted, but r6–r25 include them; that note is inaccurate. In Appendix C Table 10, the Baseline, SFT and CAA values are taken from Rimsky et al. (2024). Should those be added as rows, they must be flagged as cited results. MMLU (Table 6) shows a capability drop at α=55 (0.46→0.29) but none at α=35. No uncertainty is reported, and the GPT-4.5 judge was validated on 28 examples only.

versions.untested_parts: No harmful-user-request fine-tuning or harmful compliance/refusal rate is measured.
No ordinary or carefully chosen benign fine-tuning data is evaluated for harmful compliance.
No aligned-versus-base per-token KL divergence on harmful prompts is measured.

No compliant opening prefill, adversarial suffix, or decoding change is tested for harmful-user-request refusal. The paper tests activation interventions and a grandmother-style prompt for AI coordination.
The study intervenes on selected attention heads to induce AI coordination; it does not test whether safety behavior is localized in weights or ranks.
The study does not test whether data or training objectives cause safety to be shallow.
The study does not train or evaluate methods intended to deepen safety beyond the first response tokens.
